question: Who among the following is a famous performer of the Kathakali classical dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopinath.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Gopinath (1908-1987) was a legendary exponent and pioneer of Kathakali, who later also created a modern dance form called Kerala Natanam. (कथकली — गोपीनाथ)

 

• He trained under renowned Kathakali gurus at the Kerala Kalamandalam and went on to popularise Kathakali on the international stage, performing with his partner Thankamani Gopinath.

 

• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form of Kerala, characterised by elaborate costumes, colourful face make-up (chutti), and stylised hand gestures (mudras) depicting stories from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known Kathakali exponents include Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair and Kalamandalam Gopi.

 

NOTE

 

• Pankaj Charan Das (Option 1): He was a pioneering guru of Odissi dance.

 

• Sunanda Nayar (Option 2): She is a well-known exponent of Kathak, a disciple of Pandit Birju Maharaj.

 

• Raja Reddy (Option 4): Along with Radha Reddy, he is a celebrated exponent of Kuchipudi.

question: Who was appointed the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi in May 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vinai Kumar Saxena.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vinai Kumar Saxena was appointed the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi on 23 May 2022, succeeding Anil Baijal. (दिल्ली के उपराज्यपाल — विनय कुमार सक्सेना)

 

• Before this appointment, he served as the Chairman of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).

 

• The Lieutenant Governor is the constitutional head of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, appointed by the President of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Delhi is a Union Territory with a Legislative Assembly, governed under the provisions of Article 239AA of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Vivek Kumar (Option 1), Arvind Krishna (Option 2) and Vijay Shekar Sharma (Option 4): None of them held the post of Lieutenant Governor of Delhi; Arvind Krishna is the CEO of IBM and Vijay Shekhar Sharma is the founder of Paytm.

question: What powers the Earth's internal heat engine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Radioactive energy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Earth's internal heat engine is powered primarily by the radioactive decay of elements such as uranium, thorium, and potassium-40 present in the Earth's crust and mantle. (पृथ्वी का आंतरिक ऊष्मा इंजन — रेडियोधर्मी ऊर्जा)

 

• This internal heat, along with residual primordial heat left over from the planet's formation, drives processes like mantle convection, plate tectonics, volcanism, and the geodynamo that generates Earth's magnetic field.

 

• Unlike the Earth's surface climate system, which is driven by solar energy, the deep interior is thermally isolated from the Sun and relies on internal sources of heat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Earth's interior is layered into the crust, mantle, outer core (liquid) and inner core (solid), with temperatures increasing with depth (geothermal gradient).

 

NOTE

 

• Solar Energy (Option 1): Powers the Earth's surface and atmospheric processes (weather, climate), not its internal heat engine.

 

• Volcanoes (Option 2): These are a surface expression/output of internal heat, not its source.

 

• Tides (Option 4): Ocean tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun; tidal friction contributes only a very minor amount to Earth's heat budget.

question: Which of the following has unit m/s2?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acceleration.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with time, so its SI unit is metre per second squared (m/s²). (त्वरण — मीटर/सेकंड²)

 

• Since velocity has units of m/s and acceleration = velocity/time, the unit becomes (m/s)/s = m/s².

 

• Acceleration is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Force, by Newton's second law (F = ma), has the unit kg·m/s² (Newton), which also involves m/s².

 

NOTE

 

• Speed (Option 1) and Velocity (Option 4): Both are measured in metre per second (m/s), not m/s².

 

• Distance (Option 2): Measured in metre (m), a unit of length.

question: Shovana Narayan was awarded which of the following awards in 2013?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Deba Prasad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shovana Narayan, a renowned Kathak dancer, was honoured with the Guru Deba Prasad Award in 2013. (शोवना नारायण — गुरु देबा प्रसाद पुरस्कार)

 

• She is a Padma Shri awardee (1992) and is known for blending Kathak with other art forms such as tap dance, flamenco and western classical ballet.

 

• She is also a retired officer of the Indian Audit and Accounts Service (IAAS).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shovana Narayan received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Kathak in 1999-2000.

 

NOTE

 

• Sangam Kala (Option 2), Kalidas Samman (Option 3) and Bharat Muni Samman (Option 4): These are other prestigious cultural/dance honours in India but were not the award conferred on Shovana Narayan in 2013.

question: Medisep is a unique and comprehensive social insurance scheme. This scheme was implemented by which state government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• MEDISEP (Medical Insurance Scheme for State Employees and Pensioners) is a comprehensive social health insurance scheme implemented by the Government of Kerala. (मेडिसेप योजना — केरल)

 

• It provides cashless treatment up to Rs. 3 lakh per family per year to state government employees and pensioners and their dependents.

 

• It is implemented in association with the New India Assurance Company and is administered by the State Insurance Department of Kerala.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala also runs schemes like Karunya Arogya Suraksha Padhathi (KASP) for the wider public health insurance coverage.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1), Chhattisgarh (Option 2) and Rajasthan (Option 4): These states run their own separate health/insurance schemes (e.g. Karnataka's Arogya Karnataka), but MEDISEP is specific to Kerala.

question: Which of the following is a unit of distance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Light year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A light year is the distance that light travels in a vacuum in one Julian year, approximately 9.46 trillion kilometres (9.46 × 10¹² km). (प्रकाश वर्ष — दूरी की इकाई)

 

• It is commonly used to measure vast astronomical distances, such as the distance between stars and galaxies.

 

• Other units of astronomical distance include the Astronomical Unit (AU) and the Parsec.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• 1 Parsec ≈ 3.26 light years; 1 AU is the average distance between the Earth and the Sun (~149.6 million km).

 

NOTE

 

• Newton (Option 1): SI unit of force.

 

• Watt (Option 2): SI unit of power.

 

• Joule (Option 4): SI unit of energy/work.

question: Rajaraja I and Rajendra I belonged to the ____________ dynasty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chola.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajaraja I (985-1014 CE) and his son Rajendra I (1014-1044 CE) were among the greatest rulers of the Chola dynasty, which reached the zenith of its power under them. (राजराज प्रथम व राजेंद्र प्रथम — चोल वंश)

 

• Rajaraja I built the magnificent Brihadeeswarar Temple (Rajarajeswaram) at Thanjavur, dedicated to Lord Shiva.

 

• Rajendra I extended Chola power overseas, defeating the Srivijaya Empire and building a new capital, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, to commemorate his campaign to the Ganga.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chola Empire was known for its strong navy, extensive maritime trade with Southeast Asia, and an advanced system of local self-government (village assemblies like the Ur and Sabha).

 

NOTE

 

• Pallava (Option 2): Ruled from Kanchipuram; known for the Shore Temple and rathas at Mahabalipuram.

 

• Pandya (Option 3): Ruled from Madurai, contemporaries and rivals of the Cholas and Pallavas.

 

• Chalukya (Option 4): Ruled the Deccan region, with capitals at Badami, Vatapi and later Kalyani.

question: The abbreviation “CPCL” is associated with the petroleum industry in India. Expand “CPCL”:
option_4: Corporation of Petroleum and Chemicals Limited
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• CPCL stands for Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited, a major petroleum refining company headquartered in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. (सीपीसीएल — चेन्नई पेट्रोलियम कॉर्पोरेशन लिमिटेड)

 

• It was formerly known as Madras Refineries Limited (MRL) and is a subsidiary of Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL).

 

• CPCL operates refineries at Manali and Cauvery Basin (Nagapattinam) in Tamil Nadu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's major public sector oil refining/marketing companies include IOCL, BPCL, HPCL and ONGC.

 

NOTE

 

• Central Petroleum Corporation Limited (Option 1), Coimbatore Petroleum Corporation Limited (Option 2) and Corporation of Petroleum and Chemicals Limited (Option 4): These are not the actual expansion of CPCL; they are distractor phrases.

question: Which law, that was proposed in 1811, predicted that the same volume of gases at the same temperature and pressure would have the same number of molecules?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Avogadro's law.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Avogadro's law, proposed by Amedeo Avogadro in 1811, states that equal volumes of all gases, at the same temperature and pressure, contain an equal number of molecules. (आवोगाद्रो का नियम — 1811)

 

• This law led to the concept of the mole and Avogadro's number (6.022 × 10²³), the number of particles in one mole of a substance.

 

• Mathematically, it is expressed as V ∝ n (volume is directly proportional to the number of moles, at constant T and P).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Avogadro's law is one of the foundational gas laws, along with Boyle's law, Charles' law and Gay-Lussac's law, that together give the ideal gas equation (PV = nRT).

 

NOTE

 

• Dalton's law (Option 1): States that the total pressure of a mixture of non-reacting gases equals the sum of their partial pressures.

 

• Gay-Lussac's law (Option 2): States that pressure of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature at constant volume.

 

• Charles' law (Option 4): States that volume of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature at constant pressure.

question: Which of the following dynasty was not the part of "tripartite struggle", which fought for centuries to control over one particularly prized area Kanauj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kadamba.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "Tripartite Struggle" was a long-drawn three-way contest for control of Kanauj, fought between the Pratiharas (Gurjara-Pratihara), the Palas, and the Rashtrakutas between the 8th and 10th centuries CE. (त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष — प्रतिहार, पाल, राष्ट्रकूट)

 

• The Kadamba dynasty ruled parts of present-day Karnataka and Goa and was not involved in this struggle for Kanauj.

 

• Kanauj was strategically and symbolically important as it controlled the fertile Gangetic plains and trade routes, making it a coveted prize among north Indian powers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kadambas were founded by Mayurasharma in the 4th century CE, with their capital at Banavasi.

 

NOTE

 

• Rashtrakuta (Option 2): A major participant in the tripartite struggle, ruling from the Deccan (capital Manyakheta).

 

• Pala (Option 3): Ruled Bengal and Bihar; a key participant, founded by Gopala.

 

• Gurjara-Pratihara (Option 4): Ruled from Kanauj itself for long periods; the third major participant in the struggle.

question: Which is the most popular coal in commercial use?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bituminous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bituminous coal is the most widely used and commercially popular type of coal because of its high calorific/carbon content (77-87%) and good combustion properties. (बिटुमिनस कोयला — सबसे लोकप्रिय व्यावसायिक कोयला)

 

• It is used extensively for electricity generation, steel-making (coking coal) and industrial heating.

 

• Coal formation follows a rank order based on carbon content and quality: Peat → Lignite → Bituminous → Anthracite.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anthracite is the highest-quality coal with the highest carbon content (86-98%) but is scarce and limited in occurrence (e.g., in Jammu & Kashmir in India).

 

NOTE

 

• Anthracite (Option 2): Highest grade but least commercially abundant/used.

 

• Peat (Option 3): The lowest grade, first stage of coal formation; low carbon content, not commercially significant as fuel.

 

• Lignite (Option 4): A low-grade, brownish coal, used mainly in thermal power plants near mining areas (e.g., Neyveli, Tamil Nadu) but less popular commercially than bituminous.

question: Which of the following countries will be hosting the first edition of ICC Women's Under-19 Cricket World Cup in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is South Africa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• South Africa hosted the inaugural ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup in January 2023. (आईसीसी महिला अंडर-19 विश्व कप — दक्षिण अफ्रीका)

 

• The tournament was held across venues including Benoni and Potchefstroom.

 

• India won the inaugural title, defeating England in the final at Willowmoore Park, Benoni, led by captain Shafali Verma.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tournament also featured Shweta Sehrawat as the leading run-scorer and Titas Sadhu/Parshavi Chopra among top wicket-takers for India.

 

NOTE

 

• India (Option 1): Won the tournament as champions but was not the host.

 

• Bangladesh (Option 3) and England (Option 4): Did not host the first edition of this tournament; England was the runner-up.

question: Mariana trench is located in which ocean?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pacific ocean.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mariana Trench is located in the western Pacific Ocean, east of the Mariana Islands, near Guam. (मारियाना ट्रेंच — प्रशांत महासागर)

 

• It is the deepest known part of the world's oceans, with its deepest point, the Challenger Deep, reaching approximately 10,935 metres (about 11 km) below sea level.

 

• The trench is formed at a subduction zone, where the Pacific Plate is subducting beneath the smaller Mariana Plate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Challenger Deep was first fully explored by Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh in 1960 aboard the bathyscaphe Trieste.

 

NOTE

 

• Arctic ocean (Option 1), Atlantic ocean (Option 3) and Southern ocean (Option 4): None of these host the Mariana Trench, which is exclusively a Pacific Ocean feature.

question: What is the minimum quorum required in the Lok Sabha so that it can transact any business?
option_1: One-tenth of the total number of Members of the House
option_2: One-fourth of the total number of Members of the House
option_3: One-third of the total number of Members of the House
option_4: One-fifth of the total number of Members of the House
solution_text:
The correct answer is One-tenth of the total number of Members of the House.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 100 of the Indian Constitution, the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha) is one-tenth of the total number of members of that House. (लोकसभा गणपूर्ति — कुल सदस्यों का दसवां हिस्सा)

 

• If there is no quorum during a sitting, it is the duty of the Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman) either to adjourn the House or suspend the sitting until the quorum is met.

 

• For the Lok Sabha (with 543 elected members), the quorum works out to about 55 members.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The concept of quorum ensures that decisions in the House are taken with the presence of a reasonable minimum number of representatives.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (one-fourth), Option 3 (one-third) and Option 4 (one-fifth): These are incorrect fractions; the constitutionally mandated quorum is fixed at one-tenth, not any of these.

question: Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks are included in which measure of money supply?
solution_text:
The correct answer is M2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the RBI's monetary aggregates, M2 = M1 + Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks. (मुद्रा आपूर्ति माप — M2)

 

• M1 = Currency with the public + Demand deposits with banks + Other deposits with RBI.

 

• M2 is a slightly broader measure than M1, incorporating post office savings deposits, reflecting near-money assets held outside the banking system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• M3 = M1 + Time deposits with banks (the most commonly used broad measure of money supply, also called 'Aggregate Monetary Resources').

 

• M4 = M3 + Total post office deposits (excluding National Savings Certificates).

 

NOTE

 

• M1 (Option 1): Does not include post office savings deposits at all.

 

• M4 (Option 2): Includes total post office deposits (not just savings deposits), making it broader than what the question describes.

 

• M3 (Option 4): Includes bank time deposits, not post office savings deposits.

question: In which of the following Olympic games did India NOT win Gold?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1960.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 1960 Rome Olympics, the Indian men's hockey team won the Silver medal, losing to Pakistan 0-1 in the final — ending India's streak of six consecutive Olympic hockey gold medals. (1960 रोम ओलंपिक — भारत को रजत पदक)

 

• India had won Gold medals in hockey at the 1928 (Amsterdam), 1932 (Los Angeles), 1936 (Berlin), 1948 (London), 1952 (Helsinki) and 1956 (Melbourne) Olympics consecutively before this loss.

 

• India later regained the gold at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, defeating Pakistan in the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's hockey team also won Gold at the 1980 Moscow Olympics, its most recent Olympic hockey gold to date.

 

NOTE

 

• 1948 (Option 1): India won Gold, defeating Great Britain 4-0 in the final (London Olympics).

 

• 1928 (Option 2): India won Gold at its first Olympic hockey appearance (Amsterdam).

 

• 1932 (Option 3): India won Gold at the Los Angeles Olympics, defeating hosts USA 24-1.

question: In which of the following years was the voting age reduced from 21 years to 18 years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1988.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The voting age in India was reduced from 21 years to 18 years through the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, which amended Article 326. (मतदान आयु — 61वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1988)

 

• The amendment was passed under the government of Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.

 

• The Act came into effect from 28 March 1989, but the amendment itself is officially designated and referred to as the Act of 1988.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 326 provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies to be on the basis of adult suffrage.

 

NOTE

 

• 1990 (Option 1) and 1992 (Option 2): Incorrect years; not associated with this constitutional amendment.

 

• 1989 (Option 4): This is the year the Act came into force, but the Amendment Act itself is officially dated/numbered as 1988, which is the year commonly cited as the answer.

question: Which sector was given the main emphasis in the second Five-Year Plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Industry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), based on the Mahalanobis model (developed by statistician P.C. Mahalanobis), gave primary emphasis to rapid industrialisation, particularly the development of basic and heavy industries. (द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना — उद्योग पर बल)

 

• It aimed to build a strong industrial base for self-reliant economic growth, leading to the establishment of public sector steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela.

 

• This marked a shift in strategy from the First Five-Year Plan, which had focused on agriculture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Second Plan is often called the 'Industry Plan' or the 'Mahalanobis Plan'.

 

NOTE

 

• Transport (Option 1): Was an important component but not the central emphasis.

 

• Agriculture (Option 2): Was the main focus of the First Five-Year Plan (1951-56), based on the Harrod-Domar model.

 

• Trade (Option 3): Was not the primary focus of the Second Plan.

question: Which Indian tabla virtuoso and musician won the 'Best Contemporary World Music Album' Grammy award for 'Global Drum Project'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ustad Zakir Hussain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Zakir Hussain, the legendary tabla maestro, was part of the group Mickey Hart, Zakir Hussain, Sikiru Adepoju and Giovanni Hidalgo that won the Grammy Award for Best Contemporary World Music Album for 'Global Drum Project' in 2009. (उस्ताद जाकिर हुसैन — तबला वादक, ग्रैमी पुरस्कार)

 

• He is the son of the legendary tabla player Ustad Alla Rakha and is globally regarded as one of the greatest tabla players.

 

• He has collaborated extensively with international musicians, including with Mickey Hart of the Grateful Dead, spanning fusion and world music projects.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Zakir Hussain also won multiple Grammy Awards in 2024 for the album 'As We Speak' and 'This Moment', further cementing his global legacy; he passed away in December 2024.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Sandeep Das (Option 1): A noted tabla player and Grammy winner (with the Silkroad Ensemble, 2017), but not for 'Global Drum Project'.

 

• Ustad Alla Rakha (Option 2): Zakir Hussain's father and legendary tabla player, but not associated with the 'Global Drum Project' Grammy.

 

• Pandit Anindo Chatterjee (Option 4): A renowned tabla player of the Farukhabad gharana, not associated with this Grammy award.

question: Who has been appointed as the new Attorney General of India by President Droupadi Murmu for a period of three years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is R. Venkataramani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• R. Venkataramani, a senior Supreme Court advocate, was appointed as the Attorney General for India by President Droupadi Murmu in September 2022 for a term of three years. (भारत के महान्यायवादी — आर. वेंकटरमणी)

 

• He succeeded K.K. Venugopal in this role.

 

• The Attorney General of India is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India and its primary lawyer in the Supreme Court, appointed under Article 76 of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President and has the right to speak/take part in proceedings of both Houses of Parliament, though without voting rights.

 

NOTE

 

• Shehan Karunatilaka (Option 1): A Sri Lankan author, winner of the 2022 Booker Prize, unrelated to this post.

 

• Dhananjaya Yashwant Chandrachud (Option 2): Became the Chief Justice of India in November 2022, a distinct constitutional post.

 

• Rishi Sunak (Option 3): Became the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in October 2022, unrelated to this Indian post.

question: In leaves transpiration takes place through ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stomata.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Transpiration — the loss of water vapour from plant surfaces, mainly leaves — occurs primarily through tiny pores called stomata. (रंध्र/स्टोमेटा — वाष्पोत्सर्जन)

 

• Stomata are typically found on the underside (lower epidermis) of leaves and are surrounded by specialized guard cells that regulate their opening and closing.

 

• Around 90-95% of total transpiration in most plants occurs through stomata, with the rest occurring through the cuticle (cuticular transpiration) and lenticels.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Transpiration helps in water and mineral transport (ascent of sap), cooling the plant, and maintaining turgidity.

 

NOTE

 

• Cork cell (Option 2): Part of the bark's protective tissue, involved in minimal gas exchange but not the main site of leaf transpiration.

 

• Epidermal cell (Option 3): Forms the outer covering of the leaf; transpiration through the epidermis itself (cuticular) is much less than through stomata.

 

• Guard cells (Option 4): These regulate the opening/closing of the stomatal pore but are not themselves the site through which water vapour escapes.

question: Who was recognised as ‘Asthana Nartaki’ (resident dancer) of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam for her contribution in the development and promotion of the Indian classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yamini Krishnamurthy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy, a celebrated exponent of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi, was honoured as the 'Asthana Nartaki' (resident/court dancer) of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam (TTD) for her contribution to Indian classical dance. (आस्थान नर्तकी — यामिनी कृष्णमूर्ति)

 

• She is a Padma Vibhushan awardee (2016) and one of India's foremost classical dancers.

 

• The TTD manages the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple and honours eminent artists to preserve and promote temple-associated art traditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Yamini Krishnamurthy trained under gurus such as Ellappa Pillai (Bharatanatyam) and Vempati Chinna Satyam (Kuchipudi).

 

NOTE

 

• Rukmini Devi (Option 1): A pioneering Bharatanatyam dancer who founded Kalakshetra in Chennai, not the TTD Asthana Nartaki.

 

• Ragini Devi (Option 2): An American-born dancer who played a key role in reviving Indian classical dance forms, not associated with this TTD title.

 

• Uma Sharma (Option 4): A well-known Kathak dancer, not associated with this TTD title.

question: Manimekalai describes the story of which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kovalan and Madhavi's Daughter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Manimekalai is a Tamil epic composed by Sīthalai Sāthanār, and it narrates the story of Manimekalai, the daughter of Kovalan and the dancer Madhavi. (मणिमेकलई — कोवलन और माधवी की पुत्री)

 

• It is considered a sequel to the earlier Tamil epic Silappatikaram, which narrates the tragic story of Kovalan and his wife Kannagi.

 

• Manimekalai eventually renounces worldly life and becomes a Buddhist nun, and the epic strongly promotes Buddhist philosophy and ethics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manimekalai and Silappatikaram, along with three other works, are counted among the 'Aim Perum Kappiyangal' (Five Great Epics) of Tamil literature.

 

NOTE

 

• Kovalan's wife Madhavi (Option 2): Incorrect; Madhavi was not Kovalan's wife but a courtesan/dancer with whom he had a relationship.

 

• Kovalan's first wife Kannagi (Option 3): Kannagi is the central character of the epic Silappatikaram, not Manimekalai.

 

• Kovalan and Madhavi's Son (Option 4): Incorrect; their child, the protagonist of the epic, was a daughter named Manimekalai, not a son.

question: “A History of British India” is a work Published by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is James Mill.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The History of British India" was written by the Scottish historian, economist and philosopher James Mill, first published in 1817. (ब्रिटिश भारत का इतिहास — जेम्स मिल)

 

• The work, written in three volumes, divided Indian history into Hindu, Muslim, and British periods — a periodisation later criticised by historians for being communally coloured.

 

• James Mill was associated with utilitarian philosophy and later worked for the British East India Company.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• James Mill was the father of the philosopher John Stuart Mill.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Canning (Option 1): The first Viceroy of India, in office during the 1857 revolt and its aftermath; not the author of this work.

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 2): Governor-General known for the Doctrine of Lapse; not the author of this work.

 

• Warren Hastings (Option 4): The first Governor-General of Bengal; not the author of this work.
